# onetsolutions_hosting_cron_job (Resource)

Manages a cron job of a web hosting.

The web hosting must be active. A cron job cannot be changed in place: changing any argument
removes the job and adds the new one. Terraform refuses to add a job identical to one the web
hosting already runs (same command and schedule); import that one instead. Its line key, the
`id`, is listed by the `onetsolutions_hosting_cron_jobs` data source.

The line key of a job can change when other jobs of the web hosting are added or removed: the job
is then found again by its command and schedule. If it was removed or changed outside Terraform,
the next plan adds it again. Once the web hosting is cancelled or terminated, the next refresh
removes the job from the state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

# Every night at 03:15.
resource "onetsolutions_hosting_cron_job" "backup" {
  hosting_id = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  command    = "php -q /home/account/public_html/backup.php"
  minute     = "15"
  hour       = "3"
}

# Every five minutes on weekdays.
resource "onetsolutions_hosting_cron_job" "queue" {
  hosting_id = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  command    = "php -q /home/account/public_html/queue.php"
  minute     = "*/5"
  weekday    = "1-5"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `command` (String) The command to run, such as `php -q /home/account/public_html/cron.php`. Changing it recreates the job.
- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting the cron job belongs to. Changing it recreates the cron job.

### Optional

- `day` (String) The day of month field of the schedule: one value such as `1`, a range, a list or a step, without spaces. Defaults to `*`. Changing it recreates the job.
- `hour` (String) The hour field of the schedule: one value such as `3`, a range, a list or a step, without spaces. Defaults to `*`. Changing it recreates the job.
- `minute` (String) The minute field of the schedule: one value such as `*/5`, a range, a list or a step, without spaces. Defaults to `*`. Changing it recreates the job.
- `month` (String) The month field of the schedule: one value such as `1-6`, a range, a list or a step, without spaces. Defaults to `*`. Changing it recreates the job.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `weekday` (String) The day of week field of the schedule: one value such as `1-5`, a range, a list or a step, without spaces. Defaults to `*`. Changing it recreates the job.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The line key of the job in the web hosting's crontab. It can change when other jobs of the web hosting are added or removed; the job is then found again by its command and schedule.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_cron_job.backup
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/7c1bce85ab0b06ec"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<line_key>, or <hosting_id>/<line_key> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_cron_job.backup 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/7c1bce85ab0b06ec
```
